{{Quote|Now, Syril's father fancied himself an adventurer. It was an expensive delusion. One day, suddenly, he was gone, and all we had was each other. A young delicate boy with only a mother's love and determination.|Eedy Karn|<ref name="Harvest" />}}
A [[Gender|male]] '''individual''' was the partner of<ref name="Harvest" /> the [[Coruscanti]]<ref name="Encyc">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]''</ref> [[human]] woman [[Eedy Karn]], with whom he had a child, [[Syril Karn]]. According to Eedy, the man considered himself an adventurer, although she considered that little more than a delusion. Nonetheless, his adventurous hobbies proved to be expensive. When Syril was young, the man left suddenly their [[Karn family|family]].<ref name="Harvest" />

{{Char-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
Syril Karn's father was mentioned in the [[Andor Season 2|''Andor'' Season 2]] episode "[[Harvest]]" in dialogue<ref name="Harvest" /> based on a character backstory created by actors [[Kyle Soller]] and [[Kathryn Hunter]]—who portrayed Syril and Eedy Karn, respectively—during production on [[Andor Season 1|''Andor'' season 1]].<ref name="SollerFather">{{YouTube|video=8Fhxj0V5tGY|text=Kyle Soller about Syril's father|channel=Conmose|name=Conmose|date=2025-05-05}}</ref> Before meeting Hunter, Soller had been mentally putting together a story of his own that entailed the father leaving while Syril was young. He went onto share and collaborate on it with Hunter, who had also thought the man had simply abandoned early into Syril's life.<ref name="Secret box">{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1084979/andors-kyle-soller-on-syril-karn-star-wars-cereal-whats-in-his-secret-box-and-more-exclusive-interview|text=Andor's Kyle Soller On Syril Karn, Star Wars Cereal, What's In His Secret Box, And More [Exclusive Interview]|author=Scott, Ryan|date=2022-11-03|archivedate=20240221015817}}</ref> To both actors, who discussed the topic often in order to get a feel for both characters' lives,<ref name="SollerFather" /> the man leaving—as Soller put it—"really early on, in a real acrimonious, horrible way"<ref name="Secret box" /> was more brutal than if he had been killed.<ref name="SollerFather" />

Both actors believed the father had simply pretended to go to work one day and never returned, creating an absence that hanged over both characters<ref name="SollerFather" /> and establishing the launchpad for Eedy's treatment of Syril. That treatment was born out of her anger, disappoint, grief, and frustration. As Soller recalled in an interview for season 1, his character's upbringing without a father was a heavy absence in Syril's life and created "a whole level of Jungian psychology" that would take an entire podcast interview to work out, with Soller particularly saying the absence, combined with "the over-dominating maternal influence" displayed by Eedy, made Syril into the man he was.<ref name="Secret box" />
